data.hypothesis: With 1024 CTAs of 256 threads, the prior fused four-accumulator streaming loop checks each future element on every iteration. Processing only complete groups of four in the hot loop and handling at most three tail elements afterward may reduce predicate/control overhead while preserving each lane's input order, the global tile traversal, partial count, and finalizer organization. The candidate remains unmeasured; correctness and full-call time must be checked by the controller.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use this as context for T3 experiments, not as an isolated measurement of the four-accumulator mapping.
memory_lessons.claim: The fused two-stage four-accumulator candidate was valid on 10 checked cases and measured 0.0002950901428858439 seconds on average. The baseline measured 0.0012280938784281412 seconds but used a different computation structure, so the timing difference does not isolate the CTA mapping effect.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a loop-tail-handling variant against the fused candidate with the same correctness cases and full-call timing protocol.

data.notes: This retains the prior measured fused topology's 1024 partials, 256-thread CTA dimensions, four accumulators, and CUB finalizer organization; only the handling of complete four-element groups versus the per-thread tail changes. The available timings are contextual measurements of different programs, not evidence that this candidate is faster. The controller should validate every required size and the FP64 error bound, then measure full-call time.
transformations: Reconstruct the measured fused two-stage topology with a fixed 1024-CTA, 256-thread input stage and fixed 1024-partial CUB finalizer.

Keep the four independent per-thread accumulators and lane ownership; run unconditional loads only when all four strided elements are valid, then predicate the remaining tail loads once after the loop.
Retain the existing two-kernel launch structure and write all partials and the output on each call.
